dedupe_keys.name: building performance standards feasibility in ten us cities

description: Webb and McConnell's retrofit-lab repository publishes data preparation and analysis for evaluating building-performance standards in ten US cities. It compares offices, multifamily housing and K–12 schools with ASHRAE 100–2018 site-energy targets, using city benchmarking records from 2017–2019. R scripts clean and aggregate building records, calculate required energy reductions and estimate retrofit investment, savings and simple payback. The outputs include comparative tables, plots and marginal abatement cost curves; they are scenario estimates, not measured retrofit outcomes. Public code and cleaned/supporting CSV files are available under the repository's MIT licence, while original municipal inputs retain their own terms. A limitation is that original St. Louis benchmarking data were obtained by request, not from a public portal. Cost-depth assumptions and an equal electricity/gas savings split also affect the estimates. This reusable policy case can supply building-stock and retrofit scenario inputs for infrastructure simulation, complementing physical EnergyPlus modelling (model-energyplus). The 2023 Energy and Buildings article describes the application. This review inspected metadata and documented methods without downloading building records or reproducing the calculations.
name: Building performance standards feasibility in ten US cities
notes: G7 G7-0400. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-27; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability.
outcomes: Reusable comparison of target energy reductions, potential savings, retrofit investment and payback; estimates rather than observed realised benefits.
